Trained staff could teach community members naloxone use, document distribution, and promote the shared goal of flooding the community with naloxone under the message “It’s Up 2 Us.” This would require coordination with Stephanie Lao and Population Health. Other ideas included culturally tailored mental-health presentations by Breaking Down Barriers cultural brokers addressing stigma and challenges in Hispanic and African American communities; bringing SBCM art pieces featuring lived experience; and using the festival to launch MIHMM in North and promote Fentanyl Awareness Day on May 9.

The assistant suggested additional possible festival activities, not confirmed decisions: mindfulness meditation, Mental Health First Aid, interactive art therapy, a virtual-reality empathy experience, mental-health trivia and games, a support-group meet-and-greet, a panel with professionals/community leaders/people with lived experience, and yoga or movement workshops for different age groups and skill levels.
entities: Second Annual Change Your Mind Festival

records.text: On 2023-05-27, Carlos Albornoz summarized a proposal for BHS to participate in the Second Annual Change Your Mind Mental Health Festival on May 6, 2023, which aimed to promote culturally responsive mental health and self-care. BHS could showcase regional resources and initiatives, including Crisis Stabilization Units, Leave Behind kits, and the Fentanyl Campaign. Sponsorship levels ranged from $250 to $25,000; the $25,000 title sponsorship included an opening announcement on the main stage, five more event announcements, and an opportunity for leadership to participate in a podcast with Greg Anglea about substance use disorder or mental-health topics.

records.text: Carlos Albornoz relayed that community conversations, listening sessions, UCSD focus groups, key-informant interviews, and other engagement channels had identified a North County misconception that behavioral-health resources are lacking.
